name: ServiceIntegrationContractTest
summary: Has the developers of a consuming service write the suite that verifies the provider's API, so that the provider finds out it has broken somebody in its own build rather than in production.

roles.name: ServiceIntegrationContractTest
roles.summary: The suite, written by one team and run by another. That split is the whole pattern and the thing a test class does not show: it fails for people who did not write it, who cannot tell from reading it whether the expectation still holds.

roles.name: Provider
roles.summary: The service whose API is under test. Green says it still meets the expectations of the consumers who wrote a suite, and says nothing whatever about the consumers who did not.

roles.name: Consumer
roles.summary: The service whose developers wrote the suite and whose expectations it encodes. The work leaves an open question against this role: nothing checks that what they wrote down is what they actually require.
